answers.text:
The table is about the journey to work in the city Ardenholm in 2015 and 2023 and about the time of the journey in 2023.

Firstly, the car is the most popular in the two year. In 2015 it is 46% and in 2023 it is 34%, so it go down 12%. But it is still the number one in the city.

Secondly, the bicycle become more popular. In 2015 only 9% of people use the bicycle but in 2023 it is 18%, so it is two time more. The bus or tram also go up from 22% to 27%. The walking go down a little, from 18% to 16%, and the train don't change, it is 5% in the two year.

Thirdly, about the minutes. The train need 41 minutes and this is a very long time. The bus or tram need 35 minutes. The car need 28 minutes, the bicycle need 22 minutes and the walking is only 19 minutes, so the walking is the most fast of all.

why_this_band.task_response: Every cell of the table is read in turn; the biggest rise and the biggest fall are not selected, they are lost inside the list. The two columns are described separately, but no link is made between the share and the duration, and there is no overview.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: There is no linking beyond an opening sentence like Thirdly, about the minutes. The paragraphing exists, so the reader still knows where they are.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: A limited set — go up, go down, two time more, the most fast — keeps repeating. There is no vocabulary for proportion other than popular.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Agreement and tense errors are widespread: it go down, the train don't change, the car need, in the two year. All structures are simple sentences.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Add an overview at the start of the text stating that the car lost its share and cycling doubled, and switch to the past tense throughout.

answers.text:
The table shows the percentage of journeys to work made by five types of transport in a city called Ardenholm in 2015 and 2023, and also how many minutes an average journey needed in 2023.

Overall, the car was still the most popular transport in both years, but it lost a large part of its share, while the bicycle and the bus or tram were used more in 2023. The longest journeys were made by train.

In 2015, almost half of the journeys were done by car, exactly 46%, and the bus or tram was second with 22%. Walking was 18%, the bicycle only 9% and the train just 5%.

In 2023, the car went down to 34%, and this is the biggest fall in the table. The bicycle became two times bigger, from 9% to 18%, which was the biggest growth. The bus or tram also increased, to 27%, and passed the walking, which decreased slightly to 16%. The train did not change at all.

About the time, the train took 41 minutes, which was the longest, and walking took only 19 minutes. A car journey took 28 minutes and a bicycle journey 22 minutes, so the difference between these two was small.

why_this_band.task_response: The overview states both the change in shares and the longest duration; both columns are used. The duration column is only ranked, without linking it to the mode with the biggest growth.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: 2015, 2023 and the durations are in separate paragraphs; the progression is clear. The transition About the time is a little rough, close to spoken register.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Suitable items such as share, fall, growth, decreased slightly are present. Became two times bigger and passed the walking are strained as collocations.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses and comparatives are correctly formed, and most sentences are error-free. The remaining errors are at tense and article level (this is the biggest fall, passed the walking), and do not block meaning.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Add a single sentence that ties the duration column to the shares: cycling, the mode with the biggest growth, takes only six minutes longer than the car.

answers.text:
The table gives the share of journeys to work made by five modes of transport in Ardenholm in 2015 and 2023, together with how long an average journey by each mode took in the later year.

Overall, the car lost ground sharply while cycling and public transport gained, so commuting in the city became noticeably less car-dependent. Journey times, meanwhile, bore little relation to popularity: the slowest mode was also the least used.

The car remained the commonest way of getting to work in both years, but its share fell from 46% to 34%, easily the largest movement in the table. Cycling did the opposite: at 9% in 2015 it was one of the minor modes, yet by 2023 it had doubled to 18%. Buses and trams also picked up, climbing five points to 27% and taking second place, while walking slipped marginally from 18% to 16% and the train held steady at 5%.

Turning to duration, the train was much the slowest option at 41 minutes, followed by bus or tram at 35. Walking was the quickest at 19 minutes, and cycling, the fastest-growing mode, took 22 minutes, only six more than driving.

why_this_band.task_response: The overview interprets both columns together and states that there is no relationship between duration and popularity; this is the key finding to draw from this table. The figures chosen support the biggest movement and the sharpest contrast.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Shares and durations form two separate but linked blocks; the transition Turning to duration is clear. Links between sentences are mostly built through meaning, not formulaic connectors.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Items such as lost ground, car-dependent, picked up, climbing five points, held steady, slipped marginally are natural and accurate. Emphatic forms such as much the slowest are flexible.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The colon explanation, contrast structures and participle use are controlled; the great majority of sentences are error-free. Long sentences do not damage readability.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Flag that the shares add up to 100 in both years, and state explicitly that one mode's rise comes from another's loss.
